title: Invariant affine cover for a smooth projective torus scheme
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ a split torus of finite rank $r\geq0$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-gm-ga], and $Y$ a smooth projective $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism]. Let $a:T\times_FY\to Y$ be a group action, meaning a morphism satisfying the identity and associativity identities on all commutative test algebras [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is a finite family of affine open subschemes $U_j\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] covering $Y$ such that $a|_{T\times_FU_j}$ factors through $U_j$ for each $j$. Thus each $U_j$ carries the restricted algebraic $T$-action. The empty scheme and the trivial torus are allowed.

source.place: Agent-formulated prerequisite for Section 13f, Definition 13.45 and Lemma 13.46, printed p.272. Lemma 13.46 supplies invariant affine charts only for a linear action; it does not prove this general statement. WANTED: Sumihiro, Equivariant completion, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 14 (1974), 1--28, invariant affine neighbourhood theorem for normal torus varieties and its projective smooth special case.

proof.text: If $Y$ is empty, take the empty family; every assertion is vacuous. Henceforth assume $Y$ is nonempty. By [lem-pc-projective-proper] its structure morphism is proper, hence separated, of finite type and quasi-compact by [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. These are exactly the separation and finiteness hypotheses needed below. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], $Y$ is reduced: the fibre of $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is $Y$ itself, and geometric reducedness includes reducedness over $F$.

source.place: Tag 01WC, lemma-locally-projective-proper; Tag 01W1, definition-proper. Reducedness: varieties.tex Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal.

proof.text: By [def-pc-projective-morphism], choose a closed immersion $j:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_F^N$. Let $L=j^*\mathcal O(1)$, using [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback]. It is invertible: pulling back each local rank-one frame of $\mathcal O(1)$ gives a local rank-one frame of $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $x_0,\ldots,x_N$ for the coordinate sections of $\mathcal O(1)$ and $t_i=j^*x_i$. On $D_+(x_i)$ the section $x_i$ is the frame of $\mathcal O(1)$; on overlaps its ratio to $x_j$ is $x_i/x_j$, precisely the transition rule in the twist definition. Thus the $t_i$ generate $L$: the opens $Y_{t_i}=j^{-1}D_+(x_i)$ cover $Y$. Here $Y_s$ means the open where the image of the section $s$ in the one-dimensional residue fibre of $L$ is nonzero.

source.place: Projective-space coordinate opens and twisting sheaves; agent unpacking of the transition rule in def-pc-projective-space-twist.

proof.text: Put $p:T\times_FY\to Y$ and let $e:Y\to T\times_FY$ insert $1_T$. The projection is the trivial split-torus torsor: the action on its first factor is multiplication, and $(t,y,u)\mapsto((t,y),(tu,y))$ is an isomorphism onto $(T\times_FY)\times_Y(T\times_FY)$ with inverse $((t,y),(v,y))\mapsto(t,y,t^{-1}v)$. The coordinate Laurent presentation on an affine base $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $R[z_1,w_1,\ldots,z_r,w_r]/(z_iw_i-1)_i$, so $p$ is affine of finite presentation and separated (the affine diagonal is given by the surjective multiplication map of coordinate rings). By [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] with lattice $\mathbf Z^r$, $p$ is smooth and surjective; [lem-pc-smooth-flat] gives flatness. Thus $p$ is faithfully flat. Its geometric fibres are connected: after every field extension $K/F$ they are spectra of the integral domains $K[\mathbf Z^r]$, by the same lattice lemma. This also verifies all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-relative-group-unit-axis-factorization] for the commutative group scheme $T\times_FY\to Y$: its base is reduced by step 1. These assertions include $r=0$, when $p$ is the identity.

source.place: Definition 12.14, printed p.236; explicit trivial-torsor coordinates. Smooth projection supplied by the existing lattice-torus lemma; flatness: Stacks Tag 01VF, morphisms-lemma-smooth-flat.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-line-pullback] to this torsor and the invertible module $a^*L$ on $T\times_FY$. Its base $Y$ is smooth, separated and of finite type by the hypotheses and step 1. Obtain an invertible module $M$ on $Y$ and an isomorphism $p^*M\simeq a^*L$. Pull back along $e$. Because $pe=\operatorname{id}_Y=ae$, the composition and identity isomorphisms of [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] identify this with an isomorphism $M\simeq L$. Transporting along it gives an isomorphism $\theta:p^*L\to a^*L$. Its identity restriction $c=e^*\theta$ is an automorphism of $L$. Replace $\theta$ by $\theta\circ p^*(c^{-1})$; its restriction along $e$ is now the identity. No cocycle identity has yet been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BD9, lemma-extend-invertible-module, through the existing split-torus-torsor line-pullback theorem; composition: sheaves.tex Tag 0097, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules. Agent normalization at the identity.

proof.text: On $T\times_FT\times_FY$, compare the two isomorphisms from $L_y$ to $L_{ghy}$, namely $\theta_{gh,y}$ and $\theta_{g,hy}\theta_{h,y}$, with pullbacks identified by [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition]. Their ratio is an automorphism of an invertible module, hence multiplication by a unique global unit $u$. Indeed, in a rank-one local frame an automorphism is multiplication by a unit, and changing the frame leaves that scalar unchanged, so these units glue. Restricting to $g=1$ gives $u=1$ because $\theta_{1,hy}$ is the identity. Restricting to $h=1$ gives $u=1$ because $\theta_{1,y}$ is the identity. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-group-unit-axis-factorization] with base $Y$, group $T\times_FY$, and $n=2$; step 3 checked smoothness, separation, finite presentation and geometrically connected fibres, and step 1 checked the reduced-base alternative. Its axis-trivial conclusion gives $u=1$. Therefore $\theta_{gh,y}=\theta_{g,hy}\theta_{h,y}$ as sheaf maps on the product, so $L$ is $T$-linearized, including over nonreduced test algebras.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, identity (79), and Remark 12.50, printed pp.246--247; relative axis-factorization theorem as stated in its existing DAG node. Agent cocycle calculation.

proof.text: Set $V=\Gamma(Y,L)$. The degree-one assertion of [lem-sfb-projective-polarization-section-algebra] makes $V$ finite-dimensional: $Y$ is projective of finite type, and $L$ itself is the pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ along $j$. It is nonzero because the finitely many sections $t_i\in V$ generate a line at every point of the nonempty $Y$. Apply [lem-sfb-linearized-qcoherent-cohomology-coaction] in degree zero to $G=T$, $\mathcal E=L$. Its hypotheses hold: $T$ is affine of finite type by its Laurent presentation, $Y$ is quasi-compact separated, $L$ is quasi-coherent since it is invertible, and step 5 gives the linearization. Obtain $c_0:V\to V\otimes_FF[T]$ with counit and coassociativity. In a finite basis its coefficients form a matrix over $F[T]$; these identities say its evaluation at $1$ is the identity and its evaluation at $gh$ is the product of its evaluations at $g,h$. Evaluation at $g^{-1}$ is therefore its inverse. Thus these matrices define a rational group-scheme representation $T\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. Its action on sections is exactly $(g s)(y)=\theta_{g,g^{-1}y}s(g^{-1}y)$, by the cited degree-zero formula.

source.place: Tag 0B5T, lemma-coherent-proper-ample, finite-dimensional degree-one sections; Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, through the existing cohomology-coaction theorem. Agent matrix realization of its degree-zero coaction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] to $V$. Choose bases of its finitely many nonzero character spaces and concatenate them, obtaining eigenvectors $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ forming an $F$-basis. The cited statement gives the eigenvector identities after every commutative algebra extension, not merely on $F$-points. Put $U_i=Y_{s_i}$. These opens cover $Y$: if a point $y$ were in none, every $s_i$ would be zero in $L\otimes\kappa(y)$, so every $F$-linear combination of them would be zero there; in particular all $t_0,\ldots,t_N$ would vanish, contradicting step 2. Each $U_i$ is affine by [lem-sfb-projective-polarization-section-algebra] applied to the homogeneous degree-one section $s_i$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, printed pp.234--235; Lemma 13.46, printed p.272, eigenvector-chart construction. Affineness for an ample-line section: Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 0EKE, lemma-proper-ample-delete-affine, through the existing polarization-section-algebra node.

proof.text:
Let $s_i$ have character $\chi_i$. For any commutative $F$-algebra $A$, $g\in T(A)$ and $y\in Y(A)$, substitute $gy$ for the argument in the degree-zero action formula of step 6 and use the eigenvector identity of step 7. It gives
$$\theta_{g,y}(s_i(y))=\chi_i(g)\,s_i(gy).$$
The scalar $\chi_i(g)$ is a unit and $\theta_{g,y}$ is an isomorphism of the pulled-back lines. Consequently $s_i(y)$ generates its line if and only if $s_i(gy)$ does. Apply this to the universal test point on $T\times_FU_i$ (or on an affine cover thereof): $s_i(y)$ generates there by the definition of $U_i$, so $s_i(gy)$ does too. The action therefore maps this entire scheme into the open $U_i$, and the universal property of restriction to an open gives the required factorization $T\times_FU_i\to U_i$. The restricted identity and associativity follow from those of $a$: composing with the open immersion into $Y$ gives those identities, and an open immersion is a monomorphism. The family has $m<\infty$ members. For $r=0$ the preceding proof remains valid with only the trivial character; no nontrivial weight or positive-dimensional torus was used.

source.place: Lemma 13.46, printed p.272: eigen-sections have invariant nonvanishing opens; the displayed calculation verifies this on all test algebras. Agent restriction of the action identities.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 13.46, printed p.272, motivates the eigen-section construction. The needed linearization is constructed here from the existing split-torus-torsor line-pullback and relative unit-axis-factorization lemmas; it is not attributed to Milne 13.46 or to an unavailable Sumihiro source.
